summary: Explains how to make Deferred Decal materials and project them with Decal Actors or mesh decals, the DBuffer vs GBuffer decal paths, the receiving material's Decal Response setting, Sort Order, and DBuffer material expressions for custom blending.
gotchas: Modulate blend mode silently falls back to Translucent with DBuffer decals; only Translucent and Alpha Composite are supported
Substrate and DBuffer material expressions require DBuffer Decals enabled; mobile does not support DBuffer decals
Materials using DBuffer expressions/ApplyDBuffer should set Decal Response to None to avoid double application
DBuffer decals need depth prepass; mesh decals are expensive with the Path Tracer

summary: Covers enabling Hardware Ray Tracing in Project Settings and the features it drives: ray-traced shadows, RTAO, Lumen hit-lighting reflections, per-light Cast Ray Traced Shadows, Vulkan RT config, runtime toggling, and a feature support table (Nanite fallback, WPO, Niagara, shading models).
keys: Use Hardware Ray Tracing when available
gotchas: Requires Support Compute Skin Cache; significant scene update cost above ~100k instances
Nanite meshes trace against the fallback mesh, which can cause shadow artifacts; raise fallback detail or disable Nanite
Forward rendering not supported; dithered LOD transitions not supported
Vulkan ray tracing and runtime on/off toggling are experimental

summary: Overview of offline rendering of Level Sequences with Movie Render Queue (jobs, presets, local/remote render, basic PNG render walkthrough), Movie Render Graph (graph-based configs), and the one-click Quick Render tool with its settings and Play Render Output viewer options.
gotchas: Movie Render Queue plugin must be enabled and the editor restarted
Render (Remote) requires saving changes so the separate process can read them from disk
Deferred Rendering setting must exist in the config for an image to render
Game projects may disable Support Primitive Alpha Holdout (Deferred) to avoid its performance cost

summary: Describes the NNEDenoiser plugin, the path tracer's neural denoiser using bundled Intel Open Image Denoiser models or custom UNNEModelData networks, with runtime type (CPU/GPU/RDG) selection, input/output mapping data tables and tiling settings.
gotchas: Set r.PathTracing.Denoiser.Name to NNEDenoiser for the path tracer to use it
GPU runtime type does 4 device copies and is not recommended; RDG is most efficient
The plugin containing the chosen NNE runtime must be enabled manually

summary: Legacy guide to the Pivot Painter 1.0 3ds Max MAXScript that bakes sub-object pivot and rotation data into vertex data for vertex-shader foliage animation, with Prep Tools, Hierarchy Painter and Per Object Painter sections.
gotchas: Superseded by Pivot Painter 2.0
Requires 3ds Max (tested 2010 and 2012)
Use either Hierarchy Painter or Per Object Painter, not both
3ds Max units must be centimeters and not rescaled on export

summary: Guide to Pivot Painter 2.0, a 3ds Max MAXScript that bakes pivot, axis and hierarchy data into textures, plus import settings and the PivotPainter2FoliageShader material function for wind-driven hierarchical foliage animation and its optimization.
gotchas: Requires 3ds Max (tested 2015/2016) with units set to centimeters
Textures need NoMipMaps, sRGB off, Nearest filter; 16-bit EXR uses HDR compression
Materials must have Tangent Space Normals disabled
Non-uniformly scaled meshes in Max give broken results; do a full reimport rather than Reimport

summary: Property reference for the Pivot Painter 2.0 3ds Max script panels: Prep Tools, Render Options (texture RGB/alpha data choices and their decode functions), Vertex Alpha Painter, and Package Model.
gotchas: Selection mesh for penetration-based detach cannot have holes
Pick spline/mesh objects from the viewport, not the H list hotkey
Preserve Custom Normals can be very slow

summary: Explains Post Process Volume exposure (eye adaptation): Histogram, Basic and Manual metering modes and formulas, Local Exposure, exposure compensation curve, metering mask, speed up/down, EV100 luminance range, pre-exposure, full settings tables, and the HDR (Eye Adaptation) debug visualization.
keys: Extend default luminance range in Auto Exposure settings
gotchas: Setting Min Brightness equal to Max Brightness (or Min/Max EV100) disables auto exposure
Local Exposure should always be set up when using Lumen Global Illumination
r.EyeAdaptation.Focus was removed; use an Exposure Metering Mask
Apply Physical Camera Exposure only affects Manual mode and makes most scenes much darker

summary: Describes the Post Process Volume bloom settings (Intensity, Threshold, per-blur Tint/Size), FFT-based Bloom Convolution with custom kernel textures, and the Bloom Dirt Mask, including texture setup best practices.
gotchas: Standard bloom is recommended for most games; Convolution is for cinematics or high-end hardware
Kernel and dirt mask textures need No Mipmaps and Never Stream enabled
Dirt Mask Texture cannot be blended between Post Process Volumes
Increasing Convolution Buffer hurts performance

summary: Reference for the Cine Camera Actor: creating it, piloting, picture-in-picture preview, per-camera post process, Look at Tracking, Filmback, Lens, Focus and Crop settings, and the Cine Camera Scene Capture plugin's Cine Capture Component 2D for render targets.
gotchas: Picture-in-picture preview may reduce editor performance
Cine Capture Component must be a child of the Cine Camera Component to receive its settings
Disable Follow Scene Capture Render path if capture output differs from the camera view

summary: Explains Cinematic depth of field for desktop/console: how focal length, aperture (f-stop) and focus distance interact, procedural diaphragm blade bokeh, Cine Camera and Post Process DOF settings, optimization cvars, and the removed legacy Bokeh DOF.
gotchas: Diaphragm blade simulation only runs at Epic and Cinematic scalability; lower settings fall back to circular bokeh
Aperture does not change light intensity/exposure in Unreal
Bokeh DOF was removed in UE 4.23

summary: Explains the ACES filmic tonemapper's Film settings (Slope, Toe, Shoulder, Black/White Clip) and the Post Process Volume Color Grading controls (Temperature, Global/Shadows/Midtones/Highlights, Misc, LUT), with a recommended color correction workflow.
gotchas: Film settings should be set project-wide, not changed per shot or dynamically
Do not use Gain to adjust exposure; use Exposure Bias/compensation
LUTs apply after tonemapping in LDR and won't match across HDR displays; prefer color grading controls

summary: Describes the Window > Color Grading panel, which lists color-grading-capable actors (Post Process Volumes, cameras, Color Correction Regions, nDisplay) in an Object Mixer and edits their color wheels in one place, with collections, solo/visibility toggles, and nDisplay per-viewport/per-node grading.
gotchas: Some actor types (e.g. nDisplay Root Actor) only appear when their plugin is enabled
The All collection cannot be edited, deleted, duplicated, renamed or moved

summary: Hub/overview for depth of field: Cinematic vs Mobile methods, the near/focal/far layer implementation, the Depth of Field Layers visualization, and using DOF through Post Process Volumes, cameras and the Cine Camera debug focus plane.

Explains the ACES viewing transform pipeline and how to enable HDR display output via GameUserSettings or console variables (output device, color gamut), experimental LDR UI compositing in HDR, and hardware setup considerations.
gotchas: Borderless window or windowed mode do not work for HDR output; needs exclusive fullscreen (D3D11 restriction)
LDR UI composition in HDR is experimental
Only 1000-nit and 2000-nit output paths are implemented; film-mapping curve disabled during HDR output

summary: Covers Gaussian depth of field for mobile forward rendering, its visualization, and the Mobile Depth of Field settings in the Post Process Volume Lens category.
keys: High Quality Gaussian DOF on Mobile
gotchas: Gaussian DOF is removed for Deferred and Desktop Forward renderers; mobile only (use Mobile Previewer on desktop)
Blur size, Sky Distance and Vignette Size add performance cost

summary: How to author Post Process domain materials and add them as Blendables: Blendable Location/Priority, blending material instances across volumes, SceneTexture (PostProcessInput0, GBuffer), CustomDepth and stencil for outlines/occlusion effects, TAA jitter, UVs, replacing the tonemapper, and known issues/FAQ.
gotchas: Output only via Emissive Color; outputting alpha is not supported (use Opacity)
Use PostProcessInput0, not SceneColor, to avoid banding
After-tonemapping effects using depth/GBuffer jitter with TAA; World Position needs to run before temporal upscaling
Set default material parameters to a no-effect value or volume blend transitions are hard; Replacing the Tonemapper is work in progress

summary: Step-by-step guide to User Scene Textures, transient render targets written and read by post process materials for multi-pass effects, building a variable screen-edge blur from downsample and separable Gaussian blur passes chained via material instances and a TripleBilinearLerp function.
gotchas: Enable Disable Pre Exposure Scale when using custom HLSL with User Scene Textures
Material preview can't resolve multi-level dependencies (Missing Input error); fix with Blendable Priority ordering
Materials that write to a User Scene Texture are not blended
